title: GM MARINE NAV. LTS ALARM SYSTEM

composition.serve_who: This sheet (GMMS 108'-111b, "GM MARINE NAV. LTS ALARM SYSTEM") serves the vessel's navigation lights: PORT/STBD/STERN NAV. LT., their AUX PORT/STBD/STERN duplicates, and STEAMING LT. 1/2 — all directly named on the sheet and mapped via the engineer-confirmed vocabulary to node 690-navigation-lights. The sheet documents the GM Marine NAV.LIGHT ALARM MODULE MK3-1 (a dedicated failure-monitoring/alarm controller for these same nav lights), its indicator lamp panel, mute switch, and the relay/contactor chain (Re7-Re13, C1-C4) that both switches the lights ON/OFF from the main-panel NAV LIGHTS/STEAMING LIGHTS selector switches and feeds back lamp-failure status to the alarm module and audible ALARM buzzer. The main panel NAV LIGHTS / STEAMING LIGHTS selector switches and the T/S E / T/S F terminal strips are infrastructure of 641-vessel-control-panel (per established facts), not a distinct system on this sheet.

equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: Engineer-confirmed mappings list PORT NAV. LT., STBD NAV. LT., STERN NAV. LT., AUX PORT/STBD/STERN NAV. LT., STEAMING LT. 1/2 all -> 690-navigation-lights. This sheet is titled 'GM MARINE NAV. LTS ALARM SYSTEM' and its dominant content is the switching/alarm circuitry for exactly these loads.

functions.label: Lamp-failure alarm monitoring for each nav/steaming light circuit
functions.what_it_does: The NAV.LIGHT ALARM MODULE MK3-1 monitors each of the 8 nav/steaming light circuits (RED1/GREEN1/WHITE1/RED2/GREEN2/WHITE2/STEAMING1/STEAMING2) via Plug A pins 1-8, each driving its own indicator lamp on the ALARM PANEL IND. row; a common NEG return (Plug A pin 9) and MUTE pushbutton S25 silence the audible ALARM buzzer without extinguishing the fault lamp. A separate audible ALARM buzzer (wired via its own +/- terminals to Plug C horizontal lines into the module) sounds on any monitored circuit fault. Alarm status also appears to feed back onto the relay bank's own indicator lamp (circle-X symbol) below the Re7-Re10 relay row, energised from the same relay contacts/diodes.

flow_scenarios.path: Each nav/steaming light circuit -> Plug A pin (1-8) -> module -> corresponding ALARM PANEL IND. lamp OFF -> common NEG bus (Plug A pin 9)

flow_scenarios.state: fault on one circuit (e.g. lamp open/blown)
flow_scenarios.path: Faulted circuit's Plug A pin -> module detects loss of load current -> corresponding ALARM PANEL IND. lamp illuminates -> ALARM buzzer energised via Plug C / +[1]/-[2] -> audible alarm sounds
S25 mute pushbutton (Plug A pins 10/11/12) -> silences audible ALARM buzzer -> fault indicator lamp remains lit until fault clears

key_components: ALARM PANEL IND. lamp row (8 lamps: RED1/GREEN1/WHITE1/RED2/GREEN2/WHITE2/STEAMING1/STEAMING2)

infrastructure.system_name: Vessel Control Panel (Main Panel) — NAV/STEAMING switches, terminal strips, relay bank
facts: NAV. LIGHTS and STEAMING LIGHTS selector switches (positions I/II) are drawn as '(MAIN PANEL)' inputs on this sheet, feeding Plug A pins 5-8.

Relay bank Re7-Re13, contactor blocks C1-C4, and terminal strip T/S E (terminals 21-37) form the panel-side distribution/switching infrastructure that this sheet's nav-light functions ride on; T/S E terminal 21 is the +24V DC supply bus feeding relay coils.
T/S F terminals 51/52 continue via multi-core cable MU5-12 [10]/[11] to the main panel per established fact (MU5-12/MU4-12, GMMS 112) — cross-sheet continuation, not drawn in full here.

SIEMENS 3UG4621-1AW30 relay block (IN/A1+/A2-/C1, contacts 11-12, 11-14) appears isolated at upper right with no traced feed on this sheet — likely a monitoring relay whose full wiring continues off-sheet.
